Elena / team — adding operational detail per Kimberly’s note.

1) No-training/no-derive: we have a platform-level toggle tied to account configuration. When the toggle is set (customer_opt_out_training = true) requests are routed to an isolation lane: ephemeral KV caching only, no writebacks to long-term telemetry stores, and model-improvement pipelines are suppressed for that tenant. We can include the clause below in the DPA redline: 

   "Provider shall not use Customer data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve Provider models or model weights. Provider will ensure that Customer data is excluded from any model training, evaluation, or other model-improvement processes.

"

2) Subprocessors: attached is the current inventory (redwood_subprocessors_inventory_2028-05.csv). It lists role (inference runtime, logging/observability, backups, KMS), country of processing, and whether they have access to plaintext or metadata. We flag any provider that might process EU-data in the inventory.

3) Cross-border evidence: we can supply a PDF dataflow diagram and the SCCs. We rely on SCCs with additional measures for certain cloud providers; we’ll include a short attestation describing encryption and KMS residency options.

Next steps: Marissa will produce a redline DPA with the language above and the operational commitments. We’ll put the artifacts in the Drive link Kimberly shared.

-David

David Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
